title: Two Sum
hook: Every number walks into a locker room and shouts: "Is my partner (target − me) already inside?"

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every pair (i, j)
if nums[i] + nums[j] == target → return {i, j}

sols.label: Optimised
steps: store (value, index) pairs, sort by value
two pointers: sum too small → l++, too big → r--

sols.label: Best
steps: one pass: is (target − x) already in the map? → answer
otherwise store x → index

title: Valid Anagram
hook: Two bags of Scrabble tiles — do they hold exactly the same tiles? Just count them.

sols.label: Naive
steps: sort both strings
equal after sorting → anagram

sols.label: Best
steps: one count[26]: +1 for s, −1 for t
all zeros → anagram

title: Group Anagrams
hook: Sort a word's letters and it becomes its family surname ("eat" → "aet"). Same surname → same house.

sols.label: Naive
steps: for each unused word, compare it with every later word
sorted-equal → same group

sols.label: Optimised
steps: key = sorted word
map[key].push_back(word)

sols.label: Best
steps: key = 26 letter counts (no sorting)
map[key].push_back(word)

title: Top K Frequent Elements
hook: Election night: count the votes, then put each candidate on the shelf numbered by their vote count. Read shelves from the top.

sols.label: Naive
steps: count frequencies
sort (freq, value) descending, take first k

sols.label: Optimised
steps: count frequencies
min-heap of size k: push, pop when size > k

sols.label: Best
steps: bucket[freq] = list of numbers (freq ≤ n)
walk buckets from n down, collect k

title: Product of Array Except Self
hook: Each person's gift = product of everyone on their LEFT × everyone on their RIGHT. One sunrise pass, one sunset pass.

sols.label: Naive
steps: for each i multiply every j ≠ i

sols.label: Optimised
steps: pre[i] = product of everything left of i
suf[i] = product of everything right of i; answer = pre × suf

sols.label: Best
steps: write prefix products into the answer
sweep back with a running suffix variable

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
hook: Only the FIRST domino of a chain (nobody at x−1) starts counting how far the chain falls.

sols.label: Naive
steps: for each x, keep looking for x+1, x+2… with a linear search

sols.label: Optimised
steps: sort; skip duplicates
+1 neighbour extends the run, else reset

sols.label: Best
steps: put everything in a hash set
start counting only where x−1 is missing (chain head)

title: Least Number of Unique Integers after K Removals
hook: You have k bullets. Shoot the SMALLEST gangs first — every gang wiped out is one less unique number.

sols.label: Naive
steps: count frequencies
k times: find the least-frequent number, remove one copy

sols.label: Optimised
steps: collect frequencies, sort ascending
while k ≥ freq: k −= freq, unique−−

sols.label: Best
steps: cntOfFreq[f] = how many numbers appear f times
for f = 1..n remove as many whole groups as k allows

title: Maximum Subarray
hook: Kadane's bank balance: the moment your running balance goes negative, tear up the passbook and start fresh.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i, extend j and keep a running sum

sols.label: Optimised
steps: prefix sums: best = pre[i] − smallest earlier prefix

sols.label: Best
steps: cur = max(x, cur + x)  (restart or extend)
best = max(best, cur)

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
hook: Odometer trick: if it reads P now and read P − k earlier, the stretch in between was exactly k km.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i, extend j, count sums equal to k

sols.label: Best
steps: running prefix sum; map counts of earlier prefixes (start with {0:1})
answer += count[prefix − k]

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
hook: Walk through the days remembering the cheapest day so far; every day ask "what if I sold today?"

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every buy day i and sell day j > i

sols.label: Best
steps: track min price so far
profit today = price − min

title: Valid Palindrome
hook: Two friends start at opposite ends of a bridge and walk toward each other, hopping over puddles (non-letters). They must see the same letter at every step.

sols.label: Naive
steps: build a cleaned lowercase string
compare it with its reverse

sols.label: Best
steps: l from left, r from right, skip non-alphanumerics
mismatch → false

title: Two Sum II – Input Array Is Sorted
hook: A sorted array is a seesaw: sum too heavy → right friend steps in; too light → left friend steps in.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every pair

sols.label: Optimised
steps: for each i, binary-search target − numbers[i] to its right

sols.label: Best
steps: sum < target → l++; sum > target → r--

title: 3Sum
hook: Pick a captain, then run the Two-Sum seesaw on the players to his right. Skip twins so you never form the same team twice.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try all triples, sort each, dedupe with a set

sols.label: Optimised
steps: fix i; for j > i look up −(a[i]+a[j]) in a hash set

sols.label: Best
steps: sort; for each captain i (skip duplicates)
two pointers l, r on the rest; skip duplicates after a hit

title: Container With Most Water
hook: The water level is set by the SHORTER wall. Moving the taller wall can never help, so always move the short one.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every pair of walls

sols.label: Best
steps: l = 0, r = n−1, area = width × shorter wall
move the pointer at the shorter wall inward

title: Trapping Rain Water
hook: Each bar holds water = min(tallest wall on its left, tallest on its right) − its own height.

sols.label: Naive
steps: for every bar scan left max and right max

sols.label: Optimised
steps: precompute leftMax[] and rightMax[] arrays

sols.label: Best
steps: two pointers; the side with the smaller wall is "settled"
add (sideMax − height) on that side, move it inward

title: Sort Colors
hook: Dutch flag: red gets pushed to the left wall, blue to the right wall, white stays in the middle. One sweeper walks through.

sols.label: Naive
steps: just sort

sols.label: Optimised
steps: count 0s, 1s, 2s; rewrite the array

sols.label: Best
steps: lo = next slot for 0, hi = next slot for 2, mid = sweeper
0 → swap with lo; 2 → swap with hi (don't advance mid); 1 → mid++

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
hook: A train window sliding over letters: the moment a duplicate passenger boards, kick people out from the back until everyone is unique again.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i, extend j until a repeat

sols.label: Optimised
steps: window [l, r] kept in a set
while s[r] is already inside, erase s[l++]

sols.label: Best
steps: remember last index of each char
on a repeat inside the window, jump l to last+1 directly

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
hook: A window is fine if (window size − count of its most common letter) ≤ k paint strokes. Too many strokes needed → shrink from the left.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i, extend j, track max letter count

sols.label: Best
steps: expand r, update maxCount
while (len − maxCount > k) shrink l

title: Permutation in String
hook: Slide a stencil the size of s1 across s2. When the letters under the stencil have the same counts as s1, you found it.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every window of size m: sort and compare with sorted s1

sols.label: Optimised
steps: count arrays for s1 and the current window
slide: add right char, remove left char, compare arrays

sols.label: Best
steps: need[] = counts still missing; missing = m
add char: if it was needed, missing−−; drop char: if now needed, missing++

title: Minimum Window Substring
hook: Shopping-cart window: push right until the cart holds the whole list, then pop from the left while it still does. Keep the smallest cart.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i: extend j until all of t is covered

sols.label: Best
steps: expand r: if s[r] was needed, missing−−
while missing == 0: record, then drop s[l++] (missing++ if it becomes needed)

title: Sliding Window Maximum
hook: The bouncer's queue: a tall newcomer throws out everyone shorter standing behind him, since they can never be the tallest again. The front of the queue is the current king.

sols.label: Naive
steps: for every window scan its max

sols.label: Optimised
steps: keep the window in a multiset (sorted)
add new, erase the one leaving, max = last element

sols.label: Best
steps: deque of indices with decreasing values
drop front if it left the window; pop back while smaller than new

title: Valid Parentheses
hook: A stack of plates: every opener puts a plate on top; every closer must match the TOP plate exactly or the tower falls.

sols.label: Naive
steps: keep deleting "()", "[]", "{}" until nothing changes
empty at the end → valid

sols.label: Best
steps: opener → push
closer → stack top must be its partner, pop

title: Min Stack
hook: Every plate carries a sticky note saying "smallest plate at or below me". When you pop the plate, its note leaves with it.

sols.label: Naive
steps: plain stack; scan for min when asked

sols.label: Best
steps: push (value, min(value, previous min))

title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
hook: A calculator built on a plate pile: numbers go on the pile; an operator eats the top two plates and puts the result back.

sols.label: Naive
steps: find the first operator, combine the two numbers before it
splice the result back, repeat

sols.label: Best
steps: number → push
operator → pop b, pop a, push a op b

title: Daily Temperatures
hook: Cold days wait in a line (stack). When a warm day arrives, every colder day still waiting gets its answer and leaves the line.

sols.label: Naive
steps: for each day scan forward for the first warmer day

sols.label: Optimised
steps: monotonic stack of indices (decreasing temps)
warmer day pops all colder ones and fills their answers

sols.label: Best
steps: go right-to-left; hop using answers already computed
j += res[j] skips days that are known to be colder

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
hook: Each bar asks: "How far can I stretch left and right before I hit someone shorter?" Width × my height = my rectangle.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i, extend j, keep min height

sols.label: Optimised
steps: prev-smaller index L[i] and next-smaller index R[i] via stacks
area = h[i] × (R[i] − L[i] − 1)

sols.label: Best
steps: increasing stack; a shorter bar (or the 0 sentinel at the end) pops taller bars
popped bar's width = i − (new top) − 1

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
hook: The stack remembers where the last "wall" is (an unmatched ')' or the −1 floor). Every match measures its distance back to that wall.

sols.label: Naive
steps: every start i: balance counter; < 0 break; == 0 record length

sols.label: Optimised
steps: stack of indices, start with −1
'(' push i; ')' pop → empty? push i (new wall) : len = i − top

sols.label: Best
steps: left→right: count open/close; equal → record; close > open → reset
right→left: same with roles swapped (catches "(()")

title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
hook: A bouncer with a guest list: an unmatched ')' is thrown out on the spot; '(' still waiting on the stack are thrown out at closing time.

sols.label: Optimised
steps: stack of '(' indices; ')' with empty stack → mark drop
leftover stack indices → mark drop; rebuild string

sols.label: Best
steps: pass 1 (left→right): skip ')' with no open '('
pass 2 (right→left): skip the extra '(' still open

title: Binary Search
hook: Open the dictionary in the middle. Wrong half? Tear it off. Every guess halves the book.

sols.label: Naive
steps: scan left to right

sols.label: Best
steps: lo..hi; m = lo + (hi−lo)/2
too small → lo = m+1; too big → hi = m−1

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
hook: A rotated clock face: cut it anywhere and at least ONE half is still in order. Ask: does the target live inside the ordered half?

sols.label: Naive
steps: linear scan

sols.label: Optimised
steps: binary-search the pivot (smallest element)
normal binary search in the half that can contain target

sols.label: Best
steps: if left half sorted: target inside it? go left : go right
else right half sorted: target inside it? go right : go left

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
hook: Compare the middle with the RIGHT end. If the middle is bigger, the cliff (minimum) is somewhere to the right.

sols.label: Naive
steps: min_element

sols.label: Best
steps: nums[m] > nums[hi] → lo = m+1, else hi = m

title: Koko Eating Bananas
hook: Binary search on the ANSWER: guess a speed and ask "can I finish in h hours?" Yes → try slower. No → speed up.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try speeds 1, 2, 3… until total hours ≤ h

sols.label: Best
steps: lo = 1, hi = max pile
feasible(mid) → hi = mid, else lo = mid + 1

title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days
hook: Truck-size guessing game: smallest possible truck = heaviest parcel, biggest = all parcels together. Binary-search the smallest truck that finishes in D days.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every capacity from max(w) up to sum(w)

sols.label: Best
steps: binary search capacity in [max, sum]
ok(cap): greedily fill the truck, count days

title: Find Peak Element
hook: A hiker in fog: if the path goes UP to the right, a peak must exist on the right. Keep walking uphill, halving the trail each time.

sols.label: Naive
steps: first i with nums[i] > nums[i+1] is a peak

sols.label: Best
steps: nums[m] < nums[m+1] → uphill on right: lo = m+1, else hi = m

title: Reverse Linked List
hook: Train coaches: walk forward and flip each coupling to point backward. You need three hands: prev, cur, next.

sols.label: Naive
steps: copy values to a vector, write them back reversed

sols.label: Optimised
steps: reverse the rest, then make head->next point back to head

sols.label: Best
steps: save next, flip cur->next = prev, step prev and cur forward

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
hook: A zipper: two sorted chains, always pull the smaller tooth next. A dummy head is your zipper pull.

sols.label: Naive
steps: dump all values, sort, build a new list

sols.label: Optimised
steps: smaller head wins; its next = merge(rest)

sols.label: Best
steps: dummy + tail pointer; attach the smaller node each step
attach whatever is left over

title: Linked List Cycle
hook: Tortoise and hare on a race track: if the track is a loop, the fast hare eventually laps the slow tortoise.

sols.label: Naive
steps: remember every visited node in a hash set

sols.label: Best
steps: slow moves 1, fast moves 2; they meet → cycle

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
hook: Two runners tied with an n-step rope. When the front runner crosses the finish line, the back runner is standing just before the victim.

sols.label: Naive
steps: count length L, walk L−n steps from a dummy, unlink next

sols.label: Best
steps: move fast n+1 steps ahead from the dummy
move both until fast is null; unlink slow->next

title: LRU Cache
hook: A party line: whoever you talk to moves to the FRONT. When the room is full, the person at the very back (least recently talked to) leaves. The hash map is the guest list for O(1) lookup.

sols.label: Naive
steps: vector of (key, value), front = most recent
linear search; move to front; pop back when over capacity

sols.label: Best
steps: doubly linked list (order) + hash map key → list node
get/put: splice node to front; evict from back

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
hook: Ask each child "how tall are you?", take the taller answer and add 1 for yourself. Recursion is just delegating to your children.

sols.label: Recursive DFS
steps: depth = 1 + max(depth(left), depth(right)); null → 0

sols.label: Iterative BFS
steps: process the queue one level at a time; count levels

title: Invert Binary Tree
hook: Mirror selfie: at every node swap the left and right hands, then tell both children to do the same.

sols.label: Recursive DFS
steps: swap(left, right), recurse on both

sols.label: Iterative BFS
steps: queue; pop node, swap its children, push them

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
hook: The longest road through any town = deepest road going down-left + deepest road going down-right. Every node is a possible "bend" in the road.

sols.label: Naive
steps: at every node: height(left) + height(right), recompute heights each time

sols.label: Best
steps: one DFS returns height; on the way, best = max(best, L + R)

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
hook: Floors of a building: before you start a floor, count how many people are in the queue (snapshot the size) and serve exactly that many.

sols.label: DFS with depth
steps: dfs(node, depth): res[depth].push_back(val)

sols.label: BFS (standard)
steps: size = q.size(); pop size nodes into one level; push children

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
hook: Every node carries a "permitted range" ticket handed down by its ancestors. Go left → the ceiling drops to me. Go right → the floor rises to me.

sols.label: Naive
steps: in-order traversal into an array
must be strictly increasing

sols.label: Best
steps: ok(node, lo, hi): lo < val < hi
left gets (lo, val), right gets (val, hi)

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
hook: Family reunion: each branch reports back "I found p" or "I found q". The first person who hears from BOTH sides is the common ancestor.

sols.label: Naive
steps: find root→p path and root→q path
last common node on both paths

sols.label: Best
steps: null or p or q → return it
both sides non-null → I am the LCA; else pass up the non-null side

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
hook: An in-order walk of a BST reads the numbers in sorted order, like reading a bookshelf left to right. Stop at the k-th book.

sols.label: Naive
steps: full in-order into a vector, return v[k−1]

sols.label: Best
steps: iterative in-order with a stack
count down k as you pop; stop at 0

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
hook: Stand to the right of the building and look in: on each floor you only see the LAST person in that row.

sols.label: BFS
steps: level-order; record the last node of each level

sols.label: DFS right-first
steps: visit right before left; first node seen at each new depth is visible

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
hook: A VIP lounge with only k seats and a bouncer who kicks out the weakest guest whenever it overflows. At closing time, the weakest VIP is the k-th largest.

sols.label: Naive
steps: sort descending, return nums[k−1]

sols.label: Optimised
steps: min-heap; push each; pop when size > k; top is the answer

sols.label: Best
steps: quickselect: random pivot, 3-way partition
recurse only into the side that holds index n−k

title: K Closest Points to Origin
hook: Keep a max-heap of your k nearest riders. When a closer rider shows up, the farthest of your k gets dropped.

sols.label: Naive
steps: sort by x² + y², take first k

sols.label: Optimised
steps: max-heap of (dist, index), size ≤ k

sols.label: Best
steps: quickselect (nth_element) by distance, take first k

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
hook: k checkout counters, one exit door. A min-heap always tells you whose front customer walks out next.

sols.label: Naive
steps: collect every value, sort, build a list

sols.label: Optimised
steps: push every list head into a min-heap
pop smallest, attach, push its next

sols.label: Best
steps: divide & conquer: merge pairs (0,1),(2,3)… then (0,2)… like a tournament

title: Task Scheduler
hook: The busiest task builds the skeleton: (maxFreq − 1) frames of width (n + 1), plus one slot for every task tied at the max. If the other tasks overflow the frames, there's no idle time.

sols.label: Simulation
steps: max-heap of remaining counts + cooldown queue (count, readyTime)
each tick: run the biggest task, park it; release tasks whose cooldown ended

sols.label: Best
steps: answer = max(total tasks, (maxFreq − 1) × (n + 1) + countOfMax)

title: Find Median from Data Stream
hook: Two sand piles: the left pile is a MAX-heap (small half), the right pile a MIN-heap (big half). Keep them the same size and the median sits on top.

sols.label: Naive
steps: keep a sorted vector; insert at upper_bound

sols.label: Best
steps: push to lo (max-heap), move lo.top to hi (min-heap)
if hi bigger, move hi.top back to lo

title: Merge Intervals
hook: Delivery slots on a timeline: sort by start time. If the next slot starts before the current one ends, just stretch the current one.

sols.label: Naive
steps: keep merging any overlapping pair until no pair overlaps

sols.label: Best
steps: sort by start
overlap with last merged → extend its end, else append

title: Insert Interval
hook: Three zones on the calendar: slots fully BEFORE the new one (copy them), slots that OVERLAP it (swallow them), slots fully AFTER it (copy them).

sols.label: Naive
steps: append the new interval, sort, run Merge Intervals

sols.label: Best
steps: copy all that end before new starts
swallow all that start before new ends (min start, max end); copy the rest

title: Meeting Rooms II
hook: Rooms = delivery riders. A min-heap holds "when does each rider become free". The earliest-free rider is done before the new order starts? Reuse him. Otherwise hire a new rider.

sols.label: Naive
steps: at each start time, count intervals covering it; answer = max count

sols.label: Optimised
steps: sort by start; min-heap of end times
earliest end ≤ start → pop (reuse); push this end; answer = heap size

sols.label: Best
steps: sort starts and ends separately
sweep: a start → rooms++, any end ≤ that start → rooms−−

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
hook: Greedy party planner: always keep the meeting that ENDS earliest, because it leaves the most room for everyone after it. Count the ones you cancel.

sols.label: Naive
steps: sort by start; LIS-style DP of the longest non-overlapping chain
answer = n − longest chain

sols.label: Best
steps: sort by END
start ≥ last kept end → keep it, else remove it

title: Number of Islands
hook: Fly over the sea with a paint bucket: land on any unpainted land, flood-paint the whole island, count +1. Repeat.

sols.label: DFS flood fill
steps: scan cells; on '1' → count++, DFS sinks the island to '0'

sols.label: BFS
steps: same idea with a queue (no deep recursion)

sols.label: Union-Find
steps: every land cell starts as its own island (count++)
union with right/down land neighbours; each successful union → count−−

title: Rotting Oranges
hook: Multi-source BFS is a rumour spreading: every rotten orange starts gossiping at minute 0, and each minute the rumour moves one ring outward.

sols.label: Naive
steps: each minute scan the whole grid, rot fresh neighbours of rotten ones
stop when nothing changes

sols.label: Best
steps: push ALL rotten cells first, count fresh
BFS level by level = minutes; fresh left → −1

title: Number of Provinces
hook: Friend circles: everybody shakes hands (union) with their direct friends. Count how many separate circles are left standing.

sols.label: DFS
steps: for each unvisited city: count++, DFS marks its whole province

sols.label: Union-Find
steps: start with n components; union every connected pair
each union that merges two roots → components−−

title: Course Schedule
hook: Getting dressed: socks before shoes, shirt before tie. If the rules loop (shoes before socks before shoes), it's impossible. Keep picking clothes that have no pending prerequisites.

sols.label: DFS cycle check
steps: colours: 0 = new, 1 = on current path, 2 = done
reaching a 1 again = cycle

sols.label: Kahn's BFS
steps: indegree count; queue all with indegree 0
pop, "take" it, decrement neighbours; taken == n → possible

title: Course Schedule II
hook: Same as getting dressed, but now write down the ORDER in which you picked clothes off the "no pending prerequisites" pile.

sols.label: DFS post-order
steps: DFS with colours; add a node when it finishes
reverse the finish order; a cycle → return {}

sols.label: Kahn's BFS
steps: queue of indegree-0 nodes; pop order = answer
fewer than n popped → cycle → {}

title: Network Delay Time
hook: Dijkstra is water flowing through pipes: always flood the NEAREST dry junction next (min-heap by distance). The last junction to get wet is the answer.

sols.label: Bellman-Ford
steps: relax every edge V−1 times
any node still ∞ → −1, else max distance

sols.label: Dijkstra
steps: min-heap of (dist, node); skip stale entries
relax neighbours: d[u] + w < d[v] → update, push

title: Word Ladder
hook: Every word is a metro station; changing one letter is one stop. BFS finds the fewest stops. Bidirectional BFS sends two trains from both ends to meet in the middle.

sols.label: Naive
steps: BFS; neighbours = every unused dictionary word that differs by exactly 1 letter

sols.label: Optimised
steps: BFS; neighbours = try all 26 letters at each position, keep those in the set
erase from set when visited

sols.label: Best
steps: two frontiers (from begin and from end); always expand the smaller one
a neighbour found in the other frontier → they met

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
hook: Bellman-Ford with a stop budget: run exactly k + 1 rounds of "relax every route", reading only LAST round's prices so no route sneaks in two hops in one round.

sols.label: Bellman-Ford (k+1 rounds)
steps: d = ∞, d[src] = 0
k+1 times: nd = copy of d; relax every flight using d; d = nd

sols.label: Dijkstra with stops
steps: heap of (cost, node, edgesUsed); first pop of dst = cheapest
skip if edgesUsed > k or we already reached node with fewer edges

title: Subsets
hook: At every item you reach a fork: TAKE it or SKIP it. n forks → 2ⁿ leaves → 2ⁿ subsets. Or think of n light switches and count in binary.

sols.label: Backtracking
steps: bt(i): at the end, save cur
take nums[i] → bt(i+1) → undo; skip → bt(i+1)

sols.label: Cascading
steps: start with {{}}; for each x, copy every existing subset and add x

sols.label: Bitmask
steps: mask from 0 to 2ⁿ−1; bit i set → include nums[i]

title: Permutations
hook: Musical chairs: try every person in chair 1, then solve the remaining chairs. Swap someone in, recurse, swap them back.

sols.label: used[] array
steps: pick any unused element, mark used, recurse, unmark

sols.label: In-place swaps
steps: position i: swap each j ≥ i into i, recurse on i+1, swap back

title: Combination Sum
hook: A coin jar you may reuse: at each coin either use it AGAIN (stay on the same index) or move on to the next coin. Stop as soon as you overshoot.

sols.label: Backtracking
steps: bt(start, remaining): loop i from start
choose c[i] → bt(i, rem − c[i]) (same i = reuse) → undo

sols.label: Sorted + pruning
steps: sort first; break the loop as soon as c[i] > remaining

title: Word Search
hook: An explorer in a maze with chalk: mark the cell (#) when you step in, try all 4 directions, and wipe the chalk when you back out.

sols.label: Backtracking DFS
steps: from every cell: dfs(i, r, c) matches w[i]
mark, explore 4 neighbours for w[i+1], unmark

sols.label: Pruned
sols.time: same worst case, faster in practice
steps: board lacks enough of some letter → false immediately
start from the rarer end of the word (reverse it if needed)

title: Climbing Stairs
hook: To stand on step n you came from step n−1 or n−2. Ways(n) = Ways(n−1) + Ways(n−2). It's Fibonacci wearing sneakers.

sols.label: Naive
steps: plain recursion f(n) = f(n−1) + f(n−2)

sols.label: Optimised
steps: table dp[i] = dp[i−1] + dp[i−2]

sols.label: Best
steps: keep only the last two values

title: House Robber
hook: A thief walking down a street: at each house, "rob it + best from two houses back" OR "skip it and keep the best so far".

sols.label: Naive
steps: go(i) = max(go(i−1), nums[i] + go(i−2))

sols.label: Optimised
steps: dp[i+2] = max(dp[i+1], dp[i] + nums[i])

sols.label: Best
steps: two rolling variables prev2, prev1

title: Coin Change
hook: The shopkeeper's notebook: for every amount from 0 to target, write "fewest coins to make this". Each amount = 1 + best of (amount − coin).

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every coin, recurse on amount − coin, keep the min

sols.label: Optimised
steps: same recursion + memo[amount]

sols.label: Best
steps: bottom-up: dp[0] = 0, dp[a] = min(dp[a − c] + 1)
dp[amount] still "infinite" → −1

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
hook: Patience solitaire: put each card on the leftmost pile whose top is ≥ it (binary search), or start a new pile. The number of piles is the LIS length.

sols.label: Naive
steps: take/skip each element, remembering the previous taken index

sols.label: Optimised
steps: dp[i] = 1 + max dp[j] over j < i with nums[j] < nums[i]

sols.label: Best
steps: tails[k] = smallest tail of any increasing run of length k+1
lower_bound x: replace it, or append if x is the biggest

title: Longest Common Subsequence
hook: A 2-D grid of the two words: letters match → step diagonally and add 1; otherwise take the better of "up" or "left".

sols.label: Naive
steps: match → 1 + go(i+1, j+1); else max(go(i+1, j), go(i, j+1))

sols.label: Optimised
steps: dp[i][j] = match ? dp[i−1][j−1] + 1 : max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1])

sols.label: Best
steps: one row; keep the old diagonal in a variable

title: Word Break
hook: Can the ribbon be cut into dictionary words? dp[i] means "the first i letters can be cut". A cut at j works if dp[j] is true and s[j..i) is a word.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every prefix that is a word, recurse on the rest

sols.label: Optimised
steps: dp[0] = true; dp[i] = any j < i with dp[j] && s[j..i) in dict

sols.label: Best
steps: same DP, but only look back up to the longest word length L

title: Edit Distance
hook: A typo-fixing grid with three keyboard moves: insert (from the left), delete (from above), replace (from the diagonal). Matching letters walk the diagonal for free.

sols.label: Naive
steps: match → go(i+1, j+1); else 1 + min(delete, insert, replace)

sols.label: Optimised
steps: dp[i][j] = match ? diag : 1 + min(up, left, diag)

sols.label: Best
steps: one row + a diag variable

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
hook: Can a backpack hold EXACTLY half of the total weight? For each item: put it in or leave it out. A bitset is a row of bulbs, and shift-OR lights up every reachable sum at once.

sols.label: Naive
steps: sum odd → false; take/skip recursion towards sum/2

sols.label: Optimised
steps: dp[j] = can make sum j; loop j downward so each item is used once

sols.label: Best
steps: bitset b, b[0] = 1; for each x: b |= b << x

title: Jump Game
hook: A fuel gauge: walk forward tracking the farthest point you can reach. If you're ever standing past it, you're stranded.

sols.label: Naive
steps: reachable[] array: from every reachable i mark i+1 … i+nums[i]

sols.label: Best
steps: far = max(far, i + nums[i]); i > far → false

title: Jump Game II
hook: BFS in disguise: each "level" is the stretch you can reach with j jumps. When you walk past the edge of the current level, you must take one more jump.

sols.label: Naive
steps: dp[i] = fewest jumps to reach i; relax i+1 … i+nums[i]

sols.label: Best
steps: far = farthest reach; at i == end of current level → jumps++, end = far

title: Gas Station
hook: A road trip: if total gas ≥ total cost, some start works. Whenever your tank goes negative, every station you passed is a bad start, so restart from the next one.

sols.label: Naive
steps: try every start; simulate the full loop

sols.label: Best
steps: total += diff; tank += diff
tank < 0 → start = i + 1, tank = 0; total < 0 → −1

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
hook: A dictionary shaped like a tree: every road sign is a letter, and a flag on a house says "a word ends here". startsWith only needs the road to exist; search also needs the flag.

sols.label: Naive
steps: keep a hash set of words; prefix query scans every word

sols.label: Best
steps: node = 26 child pointers + end flag
insert creates missing children; search needs end flag; startsWith just needs the path
